### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via IEmailService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx`  _(via IEmailService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/sms-service.mdx`  _(via isConfigured (symbol, a method of class EmailService; a method of interface IEmailService))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via EmailService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via IEmailService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 03966ceae096f75c73c8fada48c828b86f86e02a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dd6f57d16e05308826b417b96148676e5587d956` — the merge of head `1fe7845d183a573acf5b188889f3f3c2791baf05` into base `03966ceae096f75c73c8fada48c828b86f86e02a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dd6f57d16e05308826b417b96148676e5587d956 && git checkout dd6f57d16e05308826b417b96148676e5587d956
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 03966ceae096f75c73c8fada48c828b86f86e02a 1fe7845d183a573acf5b188889f3f3c2791baf05 && git checkout -B drift-repro 03966ceae096f75c73c8fada48c828b86f86e02a && git merge --no-ff 1fe7845d183a573acf5b188889f3f3c2791baf05

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 03966ceae096f75c73c8fada48c828b86f86e02a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 03966ceae096f75c73c8fada48c828b86f86e02a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1fe7845d183a573acf5b188889f3f3c2791baf05`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-plugin.mail-settings.test.ts + .changeset/25065-email-service-is-configured.md

### ① Derived judgments

- **The contract.** `IEmailService.isConfigured?(): boolean` (`email-service.ts:340-365`) has the same name and zero-argument boolean shape as `ISmsService.isConfigured()` (`sms-service.ts:118`), and it is optional as the claim asked.
- **Implementers.** The only in-repo implementer is plugin-email's `EmailService` (`plugin-email/src/email-service.ts:602`), and it answers the member. Every other reference is a consumer or a structural mock, and all of them stay assignable.
- **The answer is read live.** It reads `this.options.transport` on each call (`:664-666`), and `setTransport` (`:653-655`) mutates that same object.
- **Only `LogTransport` answers `false`, and no non-delivering state can answer `true`:**
  - `makeTransport` throws instead of degrading;
  - boot propagates the throw (`email-plugin.ts:437-449`);
  - every failure branch of the settings swap keeps the previous transport, and only a successfully built SMTP or API transport is installed (`:1332`, `:1386`).
- **The settings action agrees.** The `mail/test` action already uses the same `instanceof LogTransport` predicate (`:747`).
- **The tests are real.** Each ablation leg reds exactly the four assertions of the opposite value, and the `@ts-expect-error` type test compiles under `check:test-typecheck`.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)`: an optional member on a published interface. `Metadata-protocol: none`: `IEmailService` is a service contract, not an authorable key, value, type or default, and no `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` shard moves. Under AGENTS.md item 3 as amended by ruling A (#25105 / PR #25114), a non-protocol widening ships `patch`, so `patch` on both packages is the mandated level. The head's `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` reports LEVEL AXIS ✓ against the PR body.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`isConfigured() === true` is a configuration fact, not a reachability fact.** A wrong or unreachable SMTP host still answers `true`, as the TSDoc says, so #25060's consumer must still handle `status: 'failed'`.
- **Readers that still check only "service wired".** `hasEmailTransport()` / `isEmailServiceAvailable()` (`auth-manager.ts:6033-6035`, `:8998-9000`) and the walled-owner boot check (`auth-plugin.ts:~1263-1271`) are out of this claim, for #25060 or a sibling card.
- **Docs follow-up.** `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/email-service.mdx` does not document the member the way the SMS page does. This is for the docs lane.
- **Untouched.** `content/docs/releases/`; no consumer is changed.
